explanation: It was Julie Andrews's first starring film role, and it won her the Oscar for Best Actress. Her bottomless carpet bag produces a hat stand and a tall lamp.

claims.text: In Mary Poppins (1964), Mary flies down to Cherry Tree Lane holding her umbrella.
Mary Poppins does not arrive by kite, broomstick or magic carpet in the film.
Mary Poppins was Julie Andrews's first starring role in a feature film.
Julie Andrews won the Academy Award for Best Actress for Mary Poppins, at the ceremony held in 1965.
In the film, Mary pulls a hat stand and a tall standard lamp out of her carpet bag.

writerNotes: Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a detail is easy to get wrong; the schema's riskReason list has no 'only' or 'counterintuitive', so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers film or TV facts, so every high-risk claim here needs checker evidence from the web. Rival test: The kite belongs to the film's closing song and scene, and the broomstick to Disney's Bedknobs and Broomsticks (1971); neither is how Mary travels. She carries her carpet bag as she lands, which is why the stem asks what she uses to fly rather than what she holds. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: a family film shown worldwide; the options are everyday objects any player can weigh. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 29 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json; no claim resembles a listed myth. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: c3 says first starring role, because Andrews had earlier sung for the English version of an animated film; Mary Poppins is her first starring screen role.
